column1: There is a spear leaning on the rack behind the Hunter.
column2: 獵人身後的架子上，斜倚著一支長矛。

column1: From the simplicity of the Hunter's clothing and his worn face, I would say that he is a poor man.
column2: 從獵人樸素的衣著與滿是風霜的面容看來，我猜他是個窮苦人。

column1: It is a makeshift rack.
column2: 這是個臨時搭成的架子。

column1: The hunter has several pelts drying upon simple racks made of sticks.
column2: 獵人用幾根木棍搭成簡陋的架子，上頭晾著幾張獸皮。

column1: Did you expect the spear to be here?  You were warned that it could not leave the forest.
column2: 你以為長矛會在這裡？早有人警告過你，它離不開這座森林。

column1: The spear remains wedged in the carcass of the boar.
column2: 那支長矛仍卡在野豬的屍身裡。

column1: He is clearly not here.
column2: 他顯然不在這裡。

column1: It would be best to avoid the creature, unless you have copper or tin to give it.
column2: 除非你備有銅或錫可以奉上，否則最好避開這東西。

column1: In this small clearing, a Hunter has set up his skins on racks to dry.  Next to him are three spears.  He is a bold man or a desperate one to seek his living in the Forest Perilous.
column2: 這片小小的空地上，一名獵人架起木架晾曬獸皮，身旁擺著三支長矛。能在派瑞樂斯森林裡討生活，這人不是膽識過人，就是走投無路。

column1: It is the same as when you passed through here before.  The Hunter is still here with his spears and his skins.
column2: 這裡的景象和你先前經過時一樣。獵人依舊守在這裡，帶著他的長矛與獸皮。

column1: This clearing seems larger without the Hunter in it.
column2: 少了獵人，這片空地似乎顯得開闊了些。

column1: The Hunter has left and taken everything with him.
column2: 獵人已經離去，並帶走了他所有的家當。

column1: Like a true man of the forest, he has vanished leaving no trace that he was ever here.
column2: 一如真正的林中人，他消失得無影無蹤，彷彿從未來過此地。

column1: There is no lance here, nor did the Hunter have one.
column2: 這裡沒有長槍，獵人本來也不曾有過。

column1: Your best source of such information, the Hunter, is now gone.
column2: 你打聽此事最好的線索——那位獵人，如今已經離開了。

column1: There is no use for it here.
column2: 此物在此派不上用場。

column1: If you are threatened by a boar, that will be the time to make use of it.
column2: 若遭野豬威脅，正是用上它的時候。

column1: You cannot use what you do not have.
column2: 你不曾擁有之物，如何使用？

column1: You are talking nonsense.
column2: 你這是在胡言亂語。

column1: I am sure you will find a likely bush somewhere in the forest for that.
column2: 我想，森林中不乏合適的灌木叢可供此用。

column1: I know who you are, Arthur.
column2: 我知道你是誰，亞瑟。

column1: I did not know that trees could pay taxes.
column2: 我倒不知道樹木也得納稅。

column1: There is no one here save you and the mule.
column2: 此處除了你與騾子，別無他人。

column1: From whom? There is no-one here.
column2: 向誰要？這裡空無一人。

column1: Difficult, since he is not here.
column2: 這可難了，畢竟他人不在這裡。

column1: He is no longer here, though a trace of him does linger on.
column2: 他已不在此處，但仍留下幾分蹤跡。

column1: But the Hunter is gone.
column2: 但獵人已經離開了。

column1: Is something wrong, m'lord?
column2: 有什麼不對勁嗎，吾王？

column1: I sense no danger here, but you are wise to be at readiness at all times in this forest.
column2: 我未感應到此處有何危險，但你時時保持戒備，在這座森林裡是明智之舉。

column1: The staff of this boar spear is made of the sacred oak and the spearhead forged by the Black Knight himself.
column2: 這支獵豬矛的矛桿取自聖橡木，矛頭則由黑武士親手鍛造。

column1: I will fasten it beneath your steed's trappings, so it will be secure until needed.
column2: 我會將它繫在你坐騎的鞍具下方，妥善收好，待用時取出。

column1: 'Tis done.  But be warned, m'lord, the spear draws its power from the Forest itself and cannot be taken away from it.
column2: 辦妥了。但吾王須知，這支長矛的力量源自森林本身，不能被帶離此地。

column1: I am called Hugo the Bold.
column2: 人稱我作「無畏雨果」。

column1: Ask the Hunter.
column2: 去問那獵人吧。

column1: The Hunter would likely know more than I.
column2: 獵人知道的，多半比我還多。

column1: This boar spear once belonged to the Black Knight and is powerful enough to kill even the giant boars of this Forest.  He has laid an enchantment on it so that it belongs to the Forest and cannot be taken from here.
column2: 這支獵豬矛曾屬於黑武士所有，威力足以誅殺這座森林裡的巨型野豬。他在矛上施了法術，使它歸屬於森林，無法帶離此地。

column1: We are very poor and I have five children to feed.
column2: 我們家境貧寒，還有五個孩子要養活。

column1: I have no lances, only my spears.
column2: 我沒有長槍，只有這些長矛。

column1: You see the results of many weary days of work, m'lord -- hare, fox and squirrel pelts.
column2: 吾王您瞧，這是我多少個勞苦日子的成果——野兔、狐狸與松鼠的毛皮。

column1: I notch together branches and sticks and use them for drying skins.
column2: 我把樹枝與木棍刻榫拼接，用來晾曬獸皮。

column1: That is a most unhappy looking mule you have, m'lord.
column2: 吾王您這頭騾子，瞧著可真是愁眉苦臉。

column1: I fear the danger of the forest was too much for it. That is one reason I never bring a pack animal with me.
column2: 恐怕是這森林裡的凶險嚇壞了牠。這也是我從不帶馱獸同行的原因之一。

column1: Aye, it is a noxious pest.  I give it bits of tin to keep it happy.
column2: 是啊，那是個惹人厭的討厭鬼。我拿些碎錫餵牠，好讓牠消停。

column1: Cernunnos is the God of the Hunt.
column2: Cernunnos 乃狩獵之神。

column1: Even one copper coin would be of much use to me, sire, and help greatly to loosen my tongue.
column2: 哪怕一枚銅幣，對我都大有用處，陛下，也能讓我這張嘴更樂意開口。

column1: The forest is full of terrible dangers. I survive by remaining carefully upon the outskirts of it.
column2: 這座森林充滿可怕的危險。我之所以能活下來，全靠謹慎地待在林緣一帶。

column1: He is a part of this forest, binding its power to him with dark magicks.  You must face his challenge, m'lord, if you wish to reach the Tor.
column2: 他已與這座森林融為一體，以黑暗法術將其力量繫於己身。吾王若想抵達那座山，就必須迎戰他的挑戰。

column1: Which knight, m'lord?
column2: 是哪一位騎士，吾王？

column1: Aye, that goodly knight came this way and rode on into the Forest to reach the Tor where he hoped to find the Grail.
column2: 是的，那位良善的騎士確實經過此地，策馬深入森林，欲往山上尋找聖杯。

column1: But I fear he has met an evil fate, for he did not pass this way again.
column2: 但恐怕他已遭逢不幸，因為此後再也不曾見他經過此地。

column1: I know nothing of him, m'lord.
column2: 我對他一無所知，吾王。

column1: The local legend goes that Joseph of Arimathea brought the holy cup here from Jerusalem and hid it upon Glastonbury Tor.  That is all I know of it.
column2: 當地流傳的傳說是，亞利馬太的約瑟從耶路撒冷將聖杯帶到此地，藏於格列斯登伯利山上。我所知的僅止於此。

column1: I would not dare to search there myself, because of the Mad Monk.
column2: 我自己是不敢前去搜尋的，因為那瘋僧侶在那裡盤據。

column1: Sire, a strange monk has taken up residence in the ruins atop Glastonbury Tor.  He has surrounded the base of the Tor with a sorcerous barrier and stones that speak!
column2: 陛下，一名古怪的僧侶已在格列斯登伯利山頂的廢墟中住了下來。他在山腳布下了法術屏障，還有會說話的石頭！

column1: The giant boars of this forest are especially dangerous.  Only a boar spear of the greatest strength is effective against them.
column2: 這座森林裡的巨型野豬格外凶險，唯有最強韌的獵豬矛才能制服牠們。

column1: Aye, there is a dreadful hag that turns men to stone. Beware of her.
column2: 是的，這裡有個可怕的老巫婆，能把人變成石頭。務必提防她。

column1: The bones of knights vanquished by the Black Knight are often left in the forest as a warning.  I pray yours will not be amongst them.
column2: 那些被黑武士擊敗的騎士，屍骨常被棄置林間以示警戒。我祈求您的骨骸不會添列其中。

column1: Nothing I can tell you about that would be of value to you, m'lord.
column2: 關於此事，我實在說不出什麼對吾王有用的話。

column1: What a mean and petty demand for a king to make. Leave such venal matters to your tax collectors.
column2: 這等卑劣瑣碎的要求，豈是一位君王該提的？這類貪鄙之事，就交給你的稅吏去辦吧。

column1: Forgive me, m'lord, but the tax collector came by last week and took my last copper coin.
column2: 恕罪，吾王，稅吏上週才來過，把我最後一枚銅幣也收走了。

column1: Leave that to the tax collectors, Arthur.  It is far beneath your dignity to do such a job.
column2: 這種事就交給稅吏去做吧，亞瑟。親自過問，實在有失你的身分。

column1: A strange word, m'lord.  I do not understand its meaning.
column2: 這詞真怪，吾王。我不明白它的意思。

column1: Tis an honor to be acknowledged by you, m'lord.
column2: 承蒙吾王垂顧，實乃莫大榮幸。

column1: Aye, m'lord.  So I judged from your royal bearing, magnificent horse, and the symbol of Pendragon upon your shield.
column2: 正是，吾王。我是從您那王者的氣度、雄駿的坐騎，還有盾牌上潘德拉貢的紋章看出來的。

column1: Having spoken with Sir Gawaine, I know something of what you seek.  You have but to ask and I will gladly share what I know, especially about the Mad Monk of Glastonbury and the Grail.
column2: 我曾與高文爵士交談過，因此略知您所尋為何物。您只管開口相問，我必樂意告知所知一切，尤其是格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶與聖杯之事。

column1: I am but a poor man, m'lord, but perhaps in some small way I may be of service to you.  Aye, tis a hard life in the forest to earn a few thin coins to feed my family.
column2: 我不過是個窮苦人，吾王，但或許還能盡些微薄之力為您效勞。是啊，在這森林裡討生活著實艱苦，為了幾枚薄幣養家糊口。

column1: He is a good fellow, but smells a bit gamy.
column2: 他是個好人，只是身上有股獵物的腥氣。

column1: From the impoverished look of him, that might best be accomplished by giving him money.
column2: 從他窮困的模樣看來，給他些錢財，或許是最好的辦法。

column1: You have no cause to attack his man.  If you are angry for some reason, look to your own faults and remember that a king must set an example by his behavior.
column2: 你沒有理由攻擊他的人。若你有什麼緣故動怒，該先反省自身的過失，別忘了君王須以身作則。

column1: By Cernunnos, I am a true man, not a bloody courtier!
column2: 以 Cernunnos 之名起誓，我是個道地的漢子，不是什麼該死的朝臣！

column1: I may be a loyal servant, but if you dare to insult me in such a fashion, you may find an intimate portion of yourself skinned and hung to dry!
column2: 我雖是忠心的僕從，但你若膽敢如此羞辱於我，小心自己身上某個隱私部位被剝了皮、掛起來風乾！

column1: There is no room in your pack.  The Hunter has sworn to deliver them to Camelot and that is good enough.
column2: 你的行囊已無空間。獵人已立誓將它們送至肯萊特，這樣便已足夠。

column1: They do not belong to you.
column2: 此物並非你所有。

column1: But, m'lord, you already have the spear.
column2: 但，吾王，長槍已在你手中。

column1: You are the king, Arthur, not some common bandit. The Hunter seems a reasonable man.  Obtain the spear in a manner that befits you.
column2: 你是國王，亞瑟，不是什麼尋常的盜賊。這獵人看來是個通情達理之人。你當以合乎身分的方式取得那把長槍。

column1: What rubbish is this? You are a king.  Behave like one.
column2: 這是什麼胡言亂語？你是一國之君，該有一國之君的樣子。

column1: I gave my last bit of tin to Widdershins.
column2: 我把最後一點錫器都給了 Widdershins。

column1: My racks are but a few branches notched together. Nothing of worth to you, m'lord.
column2: 我這些架子不過是幾根刻了痕的樹枝拼湊而成，於吾王而言不值一提。

column1: As you have guessed, I do carry a knife for hunting and skinning, but I could not part with it and still practice my trade.
column2: 如你所料，我確實隨身帶著一把獵刀，用來剝皮宰殺，但少了它，我這行當便做不下去了，恕難割愛。

column1: They are yours, m'lord.  I will deliver them to Camelot for you, by my oath as your loyal man.
column2: 它們是吾王的了。我以忠僕之名立誓，會替你把它們送到肯萊特。

column1: You have generously given me the price of the skins already, m'lord.  Consider them yours.
column2: 吾王已慷慨付清了這些獸皮的價錢，就當它們是你的吧。

column1: Since your mission is clearly urgent, I give you my oath of honor to deliver them safely to Camelot for you.
column2: 既然你的使命顯然十萬火急，我便以名譽立誓，會安全地替你送到肯萊特。

column1: I would be happy to sell them to you, m'lord, for but a single silver coin.
column2: 吾王若肯出一枚銀幣，我很樂意割愛。

column1: You have been more than generous to me.  Allow me to give the spear to you.
column2: 你待我已是仁至義盡，容我將這把長槍奉上。

column1: I would sell this spear to no other man save you, m'lord.  Forgive my audacity, but the spear is of such value, I could not part with it for less than the price of a gold coin.
column2: 這把長槍，除了吾王，我誰也不賣。恕我斗膽直言，此槍價值不菲，若非一枚金幣，我實難割捨。

column1: But sire, you have not asked to buy anything from me.
column2: 但陛下，您還沒開口向我買什麼東西呢。

column1: Your entire purse, m'lord? I could not!  I am not a greedy man, only a needy one.
column2: 吾王的整個錢囊？這萬萬使不得！我並非貪婪之人，只是手頭拮据罷了。

column1: I am not a man of war.  Such things are not for me.
column2: 我不是個好戰之人，這些東西與我無緣。

column1: I would not dare to even lay hands upon it!
column2: 我連碰都不敢碰它！

column1: I beg your pardon, sire, but I see no horse.
column2: 恕我直言，陛下，我沒見著什麼馬。

column1: A noble offer!  Yet as a poor man, I could never afford to care for such a huge beast.
column2: 好慷慨的提議！只是我不過一介窮人，實在養不起這麼大的牲畜。

column1: I have never been fond of mules since I was badly bitten by one.  I beg you to keep it.
column2: 自從被一頭騾子狠狠咬過之後，我便對牠們無甚好感。還請你自己留著吧。

column1: Even if you find the mule, what use would I have for a creature that would run away when I enter the Forest?
column2: 就算找回那頭騾子，牠一進森林便要逃竄，我留著又有何用？

column1: Without a horse, m'lord, such things are of no use to me.
column2: 沒有馬，吾王，這些東西對我毫無用處。

column1: Your generosity is a credit to your name, but you will need it more than I.
column2: 你的慷慨足以為你的名聲增光，但你比我更需要這個。

column1: Tis a lovely thing, but of no use to me.
column2: 這東西是挺可愛，只是對我沒什麼用處。

column1: I have heard of such wondrous things, but I will not touch it, thank you all the same.
column2: 我聽聞過這等奇物，但還是不碰為妙，多謝美意。

column1: Nay, pardon me, but I shall not touch this lady's sleeve.  It belongs to a man who died for her love at the hands of the Black Knight and I would not disturb his ghost.
column2: 不，恕我不能碰這條夫人的絲巾。它屬於一位為她的愛情、死於黑武士之手的男子，我不願驚擾他的亡魂。

column1: Nay, m'lord.  It is yours now.  May it serve you well.
column2: 不必了，吾王。這如今是你的了，願它能為你所用。

column1: My racks are naught but a few branches notched together.  Nothing of worth to you, m'lord.
column2: 我這些架子不過是幾根刻了痕的樹枝拼湊而成，於吾王而言不值一提。

column1: Though I love to barter as much as the next man, I sense that your mission is important and you are anxious to ride on.
column2: 雖說我和誰都愛討價還價，但我看得出你的使命重大，急著上路。

column1: The price of a silver coin is all I ask.
column2: 我只求一枚銀幣的價錢。

column1: I am open to offers, m'lord, if you can but make them clear to my simple mind.
column2: 吾王若有意出價，儘管明說，我這粗淺的腦子自會明白。

column1: Why, m'lord?
column2: 為何，吾王？

column1: For what, m'lord?
column2: 所為何事，吾王？

column1: Thank you, m'lord!  And by my word as your loyal man, I will deliver them personally to Camelot.
column2: 多謝吾王！我以忠僕之名立誓，必親自將它們送到肯萊特。

column1: With all respect, sire, this is not quite enough.
column2: 恕我直言，陛下，這還不太夠。

column1: Bless you, m'lord!  I will fetch the spear.
column2: 願神保佑吾王！我這就去取長槍來。

column1: I--I am nearly speechless at such a gift!  A thousand blessings upon you!  My family and I will pray for you every night and light candles in your name at church.
column2: 我——這樣的厚禮，教我幾乎說不出話來！千萬個祝福都不足以回報你！我全家將每夜為你祈禱，並在教堂為你點上蠟燭。

column1: Bless you, m'lord, bless you!  I shall sing your praises to every man I meet!
column2: 願神保佑吾王，保佑吾王！我逢人便要傳頌你的美名！

column1: May Cernunnos, God of the Hunt, bless you!  If there is any advice I may give you, you have but to ask.  And heed this warning: beware the Mad Monk of Glastonbury!
column2: 願狩獵之神 Cernunnos 保佑吾王！若有什麼建言，只管開口便是。還有一句忠告，請務必謹記：小心格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶！

column1: Listen! There is a rustling in the bushes. Something heavy approaches.
column2: 聽！灌木叢裡傳來窸窣聲，有什麼沉重的東西正在靠近。

column1: The spear has sunk deeply into the carcass. Your final blow was your most powerful.
column2: 長槍深深沒入了屍體。你這最後一擊，是全程中最有力的一下。

column1: Where there is decay, there will be flies.
column2: 有腐敗之處，必有蒼蠅聚集。

column1: Sorrow not over the death of these savage creatures. They would just as readily have gutted you.
column2: 不必為這些凶殘野獸的死而傷懷，牠們同樣會毫不猶豫地開膛破你的肚腹。

column1: Continue your search.
column2: 繼續你的搜尋。

column1: There is the inevitable aftermath of battle -- blood and death.
column2: 這是戰鬥過後在所難免的景象——鮮血與死亡。

column1: You fought well, but it is not a pretty sight.
column2: 你這一戰打得漂亮，但眼前的景象卻不忍卒睹。

column1: It has sunk deeply into the carcass. Your final blow was your most powerful.
column2: 它深深沒入了屍體。你這最後一擊，是全程中最有力的一下。

column1: There is plenty of it.
column2: 這東西多得是。

column1: Boars have deadly tusks and an evil temperament to match.
column2: 野豬有致命的獠牙，脾性也同樣兇惡。

column1: Ridiculous.
column2: 荒謬。

column1: Forget the spear. It will serve you no more.
column2: 別管那把長槍了，它再也派不上用場。

column1: The battle is over.
column2: 戰鬥已經結束。

column1: The boars are dead. What would that accomplish?
column2: 野豬已經死了，這麼做又有何意義？

column1: It is too firmly wedged inside the boar. You must leave it there, I fear.
column2: 它牢牢卡在野豬的屍身裡，恐怕你只能就此放棄了。

column1: That would be a long, tedious and bloody job. Your mission is urgent. Leave the spear as it is.
column2: 那將是一件冗長、繁瑣又血腥的工作。你的使命緊急，就讓長槍留在原處吧。

column1: Although the flesh of the wild pig is delicious, it would take much time and effort which you do not have to spare.
column2: 野豬肉雖然美味，但處理起來費時費力，你並沒有多餘的時間。

column1: Your humor leaves much to be desired.
column2: 你這玩笑開得，實在不怎麼高明。

column1: How unsavory. Even the followers of Mithras no longer practice this. Now they drink wine instead of blood in their resurrection rituals. The Christians have followed this tradition as well.
column2: 真是令人作嘔。就連米夏拉的信徒如今都已不再這麼做，他們在復活儀式中改以酒代血，基督徒也沿襲了這個作法。

column1: Your ferocious battle has driven any other boars away, luckily for you.
column2: 你這場凶猛的搏鬥，已把其餘的野豬都嚇跑了，算你走運。

column1: That would be boring.
column2: 那未免太乏味了。

column1: The normal sounds of the forest have returned, along with the buzzing of the flies.
column2: 森林恢復了尋常的聲響，還夾雜著蒼蠅的嗡嗡聲。

column1: All is deathly silent in the aftermath of this struggle.
column2: 這場搏鬥過後，四下一片死寂。

column1: The strong, foul odor of the boars overwhelms all else.
column2: 野豬身上濃烈的惡臭，蓋過了一切其他氣味。

column1: You cannot help such creatures. The giant boars of the Forest Perilous live only to kill.
column2: 這種生物你幫不了。派瑞樂斯森林裡的巨型野豬，生來便只為殺戮。

column1: If this were a hunt, perhaps it would be worth the toil, but you are on a sacred mission. It is time to move on.
column2: 若這只是一場狩獵，或許值得如此費力，但你身負神聖的使命，該是啟程的時候了。

column1: Mighty as Excaliber is, it is not long enough to kill the boar before it can reach you.
column2: 聖劍雖然威力強大，卻不夠長，來不及在野豬撲到你身前將牠擊殺。

column1: Listen! There is a rustling in the bushes.  Something heavy approaches.
column2: 聽！灌木叢裡傳來窸窣聲，有什麼沉重的東西正在靠近。

column1: The boars have trampled the ground here keeping it clear of the thick undergrowth which borders it.
column2: 野豬在此地踐踏出一片空地，四周濃密的灌木叢因而不得侵入。

column1: The boar has gored you to the core. Alas, King Arthur is no more.
column2: 野豬的獠牙深深刺穿了你的要害。唉，亞瑟王，就此殞落。

column1: That is one crow we can do without.
column2: 少了這隻烏鴉，倒也無妨。

column1: Heed the words of the crow, for it is no ordinary bird.  It is the voice of the Black Knight.
column2: 留意這烏鴉所言，牠並非尋常飛禽，而是黑武士的化聲。

column1: 'Tis a Father Tree.  Sometimes, if you are worthy enough, such wise and ancient beings will even speak with you.
column2: 這便是老父樹。有時，若你夠格，這等睿智的古老生靈甚至願意開口與你交談。

column1: Clearly, he was once a stout knight.  Naught is left but a bit of armour, his bones picked clean by the crow.
column2: 顯然，他生前曾是位健壯的騎士。如今只剩下幾片盔甲，骨頭早被烏鴉啄得乾乾淨淨。

column1: Clearly, he was once a stout knight.  Naught is left but a bit of armour, his bones picked clean by the crow, and a bit of brightly colored silk.
column2: 顯然，他生前曾是位健壯的騎士。如今只剩下幾片盔甲、被烏鴉啄得乾乾淨淨的骨頭，還有一小片色彩鮮豔的絲巾。

column1: The rock juts from the heart of the forest like a jagged tooth.  There is evil power within it.
column2: 這塊岩石從森林深處突出，宛如一顆參差的獠牙，其中蘊藏著邪惡的力量。

column1: These mushrooms are of the species Amanita Muscaria. They are very dangerous at the best of times, and said to cause madness or death.
column2: 這些蕈菇屬於毒蠅傘一類，即便在最尋常的情況下也極為危險，據說會致人瘋狂或死亡。

column1: The clearing is as you left it, but now, to your everlasting shame, this poor soul is no longer the only dead knight in the forest.
column2: 這片空地一如你離去時的模樣，但如今，令你永生蒙羞的是，這可憐的亡魂已不再是森林裡唯一的亡故騎士。

column1: I fear the lady may well have found her dead knight and it has brought her only grief.  Alas, alas, this life is but a vale of tears.
column2: 我恐怕那位夫人已經找到她亡故的騎士，卻只換來滿心悲痛。唉，唉，人生不過是一場淚水的谷地。

column1: Little has changed, except for signs that your horse passed this way bearing Sir Gawaine back to Camelot.
column2: 此地大致如舊，唯有些痕跡顯示你的坐騎曾馱著高文爵士自此經過，返回肯萊特。

column1: You have reached the heart of the forest where its dark power dwells.  It seems another unfortunate soul was here before you.
column2: 你已抵達森林深處，這股黑暗力量的所在。看來在你之前，還有另一個不幸的靈魂曾到過此地。

column1: Only his bare bones remain, rattling in their shell of iron.
column2: 只剩下光禿禿的骸骨，在鐵甲的軀殼裡喀啦作響。

column1: There is a piece of brightly colored silk tucked inside the armour.
column2: 盔甲裡塞著一片色彩鮮豔的絲巾。

column1: There is nothing to gain by that.
column2: 這麼做並無所得。

column1: He is the evil power that makes this forest so perilous.
column2: 他正是讓這座森林如此凶險的邪惡力量。

column1: Once it was fine metal, now it is rusted and useless.
column2: 它曾是精良的金屬，如今已鏽蝕不堪，毫無用處。

column1: The piece of silk was a lady's sleeve, a token to wear into battle.  We can only wonder what sad story was his, what favour he sought to win, and the sorrowful fate of the lady that may have awaited him with fading hope.
column2: 這片絲巾是一位夫人的衣袖，是他佩戴上戰場的信物。我們只能猜想，他有著怎樣悲傷的故事、渴望贏得誰的青睞，還有那位懷抱漸漸消逝的希望等待著他的夫人，又遭逢了何等悲涼的命運。

column1: You cannot see what is not there.
column2: 不存在的東西，你看不見。

column1: They are of the species Amanita Muscaria, a very dangerous mushroom at the best of times, said to cause madness or death.
column2: 它們屬於毒蠅傘一類，即便在最尋常的情況下也極為危險，據說會致人瘋狂或死亡。

column1: But here in the Forest Perilous, they are doubly dangerous.  For if you so much as touch these mushrooms, you will be compelled to eat them.
column2: 但在派瑞樂斯森林裡，它們危險加倍——只要你一碰觸這些蕈菇，便會身不由己地把它們吃下肚。

column1: There are no flowers nearby--only mushrooms.
column2: 附近沒有花，只有蕈菇。

column1: It cannot be moved.
column2: 它無法被移動。

column1: It juts from the heart of the forest like a jagged tooth.  There is evil power within it.
column2: 它從森林深處突出，宛如一顆參差的獠牙，其中蘊藏著邪惡的力量。

column1: Most of the trees here are quite ordinary, but this one hoary, leafless tree may well be the eldest of them all.
column2: 這裡的樹大多平凡無奇，唯獨這株灰白、落盡了葉的老樹，很可能是其中最古老的一株。

column1: It will be a grievous moment when Lady Elayne find the remains of her beloved knight.
column2: 當艾蓮公主找到她心愛騎士的遺骸時，那將是何等椎心之痛的一刻。

column1: You already have a sleeve.
column2: 你已經有一條絲巾了。

column1: You cannot get what is not there.
column2: 不存在的東西，你拿不到。

column1: Odd.  Although this lady's sleeve has surely been here as long as the dead knight, it is as new as the day the lady wore it.  There is magick involved here.
column2: 奇怪。這條夫人的絲巾理應和亡故的騎士一同留在此地已久，卻新得彷彿夫人才剛佩戴過一般，其中必有魔法在作祟。

column1: Your arms are not quite that long.
column2: 你的手臂沒有那麼長。

column1: He said all he needed to say.  He will return nevermore.
column2: 他該說的話都已說完，不會再回來了。

column1: Who dares to speak to Old Father Tree? You are but a twinkle in time, mortal.  Let me sleep the long and dreamless sleep of deep roots and sun on branch.
column2: 何人膽敢與老父樹交談？凡人啊，你不過是時光中一閃即逝的微光。且讓我沉入那深根與枝頭陽光交織的漫長無夢之眠吧。

column1: Do not disturb him further, Arthur.  He is an old and weary tree.
column2: 別再驚擾他了，亞瑟。他是一株年邁而疲憊的樹。

column1: That would not be much of a conversation.
column2: 那算不上什麼交談。

column1: If you are greeting the dead knight, I fear he has long since ceased to care about such things.
column2: 你若是在向亡故的騎士問候，恐怕他早已不再在意這些事了。

column1: They are dangerous.  Leave them be.
column2: 它們很危險，別去招惹。

column1: I warn you most strongly, the merest touch of these mushrooms will compel you to eat them with the most dire results.
column2: 我要嚴正警告你，這些蕈菇哪怕只是輕輕一碰，都會逼得你把它們吃下肚，後果不堪設想。

column1: There is no need to desecrate this poor dead knight.
column2: 沒有必要褻瀆這位可憐的亡故騎士。

column1: Long has this unfortunate knight lain here, but you have not the time now to do him such a service.
column2: 這位不幸的騎士已在此長眠許久，但你此刻沒有時間為他做這件事。

column1: This unfortunate knight is beyond your ability to help or hinder.
column2: 這位不幸的騎士，已非你的能力所能相助或妨礙。

column1: The dead knight's armour is old and rusted and of no use to you.
column2: 亡故騎士的盔甲已老舊鏽蝕，對你毫無用處。

column1: It would be futile to try.
column2: 嘗試也是徒勞。

column1: He is gone, as I would hope you noticed.
column2: 他已經走了，我想你也該注意到了。

column1: This stone would defy you.  You are well advised to leave it alone.
column2: 這塊石頭會與你對抗，你最好別去招惹它。

column1: That is beyond your power or mine.
column2: 這已超出你我的能力範圍。

column1: The knight has been dead far too long to be a threat to you.
column2: 這位騎士死去已久，早已構不成任何威脅。

column1: Rawk!  I have no need for mortal toys.
column2: 呱！凡人的玩物，我用不著。

column1: I doubt the dead knight has any interest in it.
column2: 我看那位亡故的騎士，對此不會有什麼興趣。

column1: He is long past help, Arthur.
column2: 他早已無法可救了，亞瑟。

column1: Rarawk!  Try it if you dare.  You will never touch me.
column2: 呱啦！有膽你就試試看，你永遠碰不到我。

column1: The creature deserves it, but is not here for the attempt.
column2: 這畜生是罪有應得，只是牠此刻並不在此，由不得你動手。

column1: O Fool, you seek death by coming here.  Turn back now or die!
column2: 愚者啊，你來到此地，便是自尋死路。速速回頭，否則便是一死！

column1: Hear me, then, O Brave Fool.  The Black Knight is the greatest of all knights.  None have beaten him.  He is invincible.  Even Sir Gawaine was grievously wounded.
column2: 那便聽好了，勇敢的愚者。黑武士是天下第一的騎士，從無人能勝過他，他所向無敵。就連高文爵士也被他重創。

column1: The Black Knight awaits you for a joust to the death.  Do you accept the challenge?
column2: 黑武士正等著與你來一場生死決鬥。你可願接受挑戰？

column1: Then you must turn back, for you cannot pass this way through the forest without facing the Black Knight.
column2: 那你便得回頭，因為不與黑武士一戰，你休想從這條路穿越森林。

column1: Crawk!  I shall delight in feeding on your bones when the Black Knight has finished with you!  I shall pluck out your eyes and peck at your bloody heart!
column2: 嘎呱！待黑武士收拾了你，我便能歡歡喜喜地啃食你的骨頭！我要啄出你的雙眼，啄食你血淋淋的心臟！

column1: I have no time to waste on fools.  Turn back now or face him and die.
column2: 我沒空浪費在愚者身上，快回頭，否則便去見他，一死了之。

column1: Would I tell such a fool as you even if I knew?
column2: 就算我知道，我又何必告訴你這樣的愚人？

column1: He is a prisoner of the Black Knight and dies slowly of the wounds he received.
column2: 他是黑武士的階下囚，正因所受的傷勢緩緩步向死亡。

column1: I know nothing of this knight.  Another fool like Gawaine and you, no doubt.
column2: 我對這位騎士一無所知。想必又是個像高文和你這樣的傻子。

column1: It will not answer.  It is sent by the Black Knight to taunt you, nothing more.
column2: 牠不會回應。牠是黑武士派來嘲弄你的，僅此而已。

column1: You must answer the crow, Arthur.
column2: 你必須回應那隻烏鴉，亞瑟。

column1: Of all the stubborn fools there be, I never saw such a fool as thee, You shall keep yon knight good company, And nourish the roots of Old Father Tree.
column2: 天下冥頑之徒何其多，卻不曾見過你這般執迷不悟；你將與那騎士結伴長眠，去滋養老父樹深埋的根。

column1: There is no escape, unless I allow you to pass.  But the price of safe passage is high indeed.
column2: 此地無法脫逃，除非我允你通行。但安然通行的代價著實高昂。

column1: Waste no time with empty words of politeness.
column2: 莫要浪費時間在虛情假意的客套話上。

column1: That is not within your power.
column2: 那不在你的能力範圍之內。

column1: You cannot joust with a sword.  If you accept the joust, he must perforce provide you with a jousting lance.
column2: 你不能用劍進行馬上比武。若你接受比武，他勢必得為你備妥一支比武用的長槍。

column1: By this, I assume you mean a jousting lance.
column2: 如此看來，我猜你指的是一支比武用的長槍。

column1: Were I with you in person, I could overcome this spell, but this is your mission and you alone must make the choices and seek the path to the Grail.
column2: 若我能親自隨你在此，或許能破除這道咒法，但這是你的使命，唯有你能自行抉擇、尋得通往聖杯的道路。

column1: I have no use for money.
column2: 我用不著錢財。

column1: I have no use for it.
column2: 我用不著這個。

column1: For that insult, I shall take special pleasure in slaying you.
column2: 為了這番侮辱，我將格外樂於取你性命。

column1: I will give you my ultimatum soon enough.
column2: 我很快便會向你下最後通牒。

column1: Not even I know where the Grail is hidden.
column2: 就連我也不知聖杯藏於何處。

column1: He is my prisoner.
column2: 他是我的階下囚。

column1: I know nothing about this knight.
column2: 我對這位騎士一無所知。

column1: My crow warned you.  You should have heeded the warning.
column2: 我的烏鴉早已警告過你，你本該聽從那警告的。

column1: I am the Black Knight, fool.
column2: 我便是黑武士，蠢貨。

column1: I have no equal in jousting.  You shall surely die.
column2: 馬上比武無人能與我匹敵，你必死無疑。

column1: The black knight does not respond.
column2: 黑武士並未回應。

column1: You disgust me.
column2: 你令我作嘔。

column1: Praise all the powers that be! You are victorious, my king.
column2: 讚頌一切神明的力量！吾王，你得勝了。

column1: This is no natural foe.  Nothing can be seen inside his dark, bat-winged helm and his voice is like an echo from the grave.
column2: 這絕非凡俗之敵。他那頂飾有蝙蝠翼的黑色頭盔內漆黑一片，什麼也看不見，聲音則彷彿來自墳塋深處的回響。

column1: The Black Knight has caused a hedge to grow into a natural jousting lane divider.
column2: 黑武士使一道樹籬生長成天然的比武賽道分隔。

column1: The Black Knight is gone.
column2: 黑武士已然離去。

column1: Hurry on, Arthur! Gawaine must be close by!
column2: 快走，亞瑟！高文必定就在附近！

column1: What advice can I give a fool?
column2: 我能給一個蠢貨什麼忠告？

column1: You must joust the Black Knight if you would save Gawaine.
column2: 你若想救高文，就必須與黑武士一決比武。

column1: Your foe awaits you at the other end of this jousting hedge.
column2: 你的對手正在這道比武樹籬的另一端等著你。

column1: The Black Knight's body has vanished, as is to be expected with such a supernatural being.
column2: 黑武士的軀體已然消失，這等超凡之物，如此結局本在意料之中。

column1: Only the jousting hedge remains as proof that the Black Knight was ever here.
column2: 唯有那道比武樹籬留下，證明黑武士確曾在此。

column1: You have seen the last of him.
column2: 你已見過他最後一面。

column1: He bears no special device.
column2: 他身上並無特殊的紋章。

column1: I see nothing here but forest and hedge.
column2: 我在此處除了森林與樹籬，什麼也沒看見。

column1: His helmet is adorned with two bat-like wings.
column2: 他的頭盔飾有兩片狀似蝙蝠翼的裝飾。

column1: There is nothing to be seen there.
column2: 那裡什麼也看不見。

column1: The jousting lane on the other side is exactly the same.  The Black Knight has not taken any unfair advantage.
column2: 另一側的比武賽道與此處完全相同，黑武士並未佔任何不公的便宜。

column1: It is the same as this side.
column2: 與這一側相同。

column1: It takes two to joust.
column2: 比武需要兩人方能成局。

column1: You will pass unmolested, thanks to your cowardice. I do not know how you can bear the shame of it.
column2: 憑著你的懦弱，你將得以安然通過。我實在不明白，你如何承受得起這份恥辱。

column1: The Black Knight is vanquished.  There is no need to escape.
column2: 黑武士已被擊敗，無須再逃。

column1: The Black Knight is gone and left nothing behind.
column2: 黑武士已經離去，未留下任何東西。

column1: You will not find one here.
column2: 此處找不到那樣東西。

column1: That you can only do if you defeat the Black Knight.
column2: 唯有擊敗黑武士，你才能這麼做。

column1: You have a chance now to save Gawaine.  Do not delay!
column2: 你現在有機會救出高文，切莫遲疑！

column1: You have done all you could.  His fate is no longer in your hands, but that of Camelot is.  Seek the Grail.
column2: 你已盡了全力，他的命運已不再操於你手，但肯萊特的命運仍是。去尋找聖杯吧。

column1: You can try, King Arthur, as others have died trying.
column2: 你儘管一試，亞瑟王，正如許多人曾因此一試而喪命。

column1: You have already won your victory.
column2: 你已然贏得了這場勝利。

column1: Too late for a show of bravado now.  The evil deed is done.
column2: 此刻逞英雄已為時已晚，惡行已然鑄成。

column1: Your sword is of no use here.  The Black Knight has set the terms of combat as a joust.
column2: 你的劍在此無用武之地。黑武士已定下以馬上比武決勝負的條件。

column1: Hold, King Arthur.  Do not seek to move.  Not even Merlin can free you from my power in this place.
column2: 且慢，亞瑟王。休要妄動。在此地，就連梅林也無法將你從我的力量中解救出來。

column1: Here are your choices.
column2: 這是你的選擇。

column1: In the forest beyond me, I have imprisoned your friend, Sir Gawaine.  He is sorely injured and shall die soon without help.  To free him, you must joust with me.
column2: 在我身後的森林裡，囚著你的摯友，高文爵士。他傷勢慘重，若無人相助，不久便將喪命。要救他，你必須與我比武。

column1: Three times you must unhorse me before I can die.  Three times must I unhorse you to slay you.  The first knight to strike the third blow is the victor. No matter who wins, Gawaine will go free.
column2: 你須將我三度擊落馬下，我方能一死；我也須三度將你擊落馬下，方能取你性命。誰先擊出第三擊，誰便是勝者。無論誰勝，高文都將獲釋。

column1: But if you joust with me, you will surely die.  Therefore I give you one other choice:  I will let you pass untouched.....but I will take Gawaine's life in exchange.
column2: 但若你與我比武，你必死無疑。因此我給你另一個選擇：我可讓你安然通過……但代價是高文的性命。

column1: I lay the challenge before you.  Will you joust with me for the life of Sir Gawaine?
column2: 我在此向你下戰帖。你可願為高文爵士的性命，與我一戰？

column1: Will you joust with me? Answer aye or nay.
column2: 你可願與我比武？請輸入「aye」或「nay」作答。

column1: You are a weakling and a coward.  Gawaine's life is mine and you are free to go.
column2: 你是個弱者，也是個懦夫。高文的性命歸我了，你可自行離去。

column1: Will you joust with me? Answer aye or nay.  You have no other choices.
column2: 你可願與我比武？請輸入「aye」或「nay」作答，你別無他選。

column1: You are held fast by the power of the Black Knight.
column2: 你被黑武士的力量牢牢禁錮住了。

column1: You are a worthy opponent.  Take up your lance and let the joust begin!
column2: 你是個夠格的對手。持起你的長槍，比武開始！

column1: Dead men tell no tales.
column2: 死人不會洩露秘密。

column1: Though I....did not reach the Tor....I believe it is in the possession.....of the Mad Monk of Glastonbury.
column2: 雖然我……未能抵達那座山……我相信它落在……格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶手中。

column1: Alas....I have not seen or heard of him since I left Camelot.
column2: 唉……自我離開肯萊特後，便再也沒見過他，也沒聽過他的消息。

column1: Though I....did not reach the Tor....I believe the Grail is held.....by the Mad Monk of Glastonbury.
column2: 雖然我……未能抵達那座山……我相信聖杯落在……格列斯登伯利的瘋僧侶手中。

column1: Ah...my story is not a happy one. To be defeated....by the Black Knight....I cannot bear to speak of it yet.
column2: 啊……我的遭遇並不順遂。竟敗在……黑武士手下……我此刻還無法對此啟齒。

column1: Please, M'lord.  You must continue on with your quest.
column2: 求求你，吾王。你必須繼續你的探尋。

column1: Now that you have saved Gawaine, concentrate once more upon your search.
column2: 如今你已救出高文，該再度專心於你的尋索之上了。

column1: Gawaine is close to death and urgently needs help.
column2: 高文命在旦夕，亟需援手。

column1: You let Gawaine die. I have nothing to give you at this moment but contempt.
column2: 你任由高文死去。此刻我除了鄙夷，再也給不了你別的。

column1: This place should look familiar. It was here that you freed Gawaine and sent him back to Camelot.
column2: 這地方你應當眼熟。正是在此處，你救出了高文，並送他回肯萊特。

column1: Gawaine's injuries are serious. Only the physicians of Camelot may be able to save him.
column2: 高文傷勢嚴重，唯有肯萊特的醫師或許還能救他。

column1: In spite of his injuries, Gawaine has been left shackled to a massive tree.  The Black Knight shows little mercy.
column2: 高文雖已負傷，卻仍被鎖鏈拴在一株巨樹之上，黑武士毫不留情。

column1: Naught but the proof of your shame awaits you here.  The massive tree before you marks the place where Gawaine's bones shall lie.
column2: 此處只餘你恥辱的證明。眼前這株巨樹，便是高文屍骨將要長眠之地。

column1: He is not here.
column2: 他不在這裡。

column1: The Black Knight still rules supreme in this forest, thanks to your cowardice.
column2: 拜你的懦弱所賜，黑武士依舊在這片森林裡稱王稱霸。

column1: You have vanquished him, to your great glory.
column2: 你已擊敗了他，這是你莫大的榮耀。

column1: The shackles are made of metal, sunk too deeply into the tree to pull them free, but the metal itself is not thick.
column2: 這鎖鏈是金屬打造的，深深嵌入樹身，難以硬拔脫離，但金屬本身並不厚實。

column1: The remains of the shackles shall serve as a reminder of suffering ended.
column2: 這殘留的鎖鏈，將成為苦難已然終結的提醒。

column1: He is safe.  Worry not.
column2: 他安然無恙，不必擔心。

column1: I am so filled with contempt that you allowed your great friend and noble knight to die, that I can offer you no words of wisdom or comfort.
column2: 你竟任由摯友、那位高貴的騎士死去，我心中滿是鄙夷，再也給不出任何忠告或慰藉之言。

column1: The most important thing to do is see that Gawaine reaches Camelot as quickly as possible.  But you must continue to search for the Grail.
column2: 眼下最要緊的，是設法讓高文儘快抵達肯萊特。但你仍須繼續尋找聖杯。

column1: Gawaine is gone.
column2: 高文已經不在了。

column1: Gawaine is still alive, barely.  Hanging from the shackles must pain him cruelly.
column2: 高文尚存一息，僅此而已。懸吊在這鎖鏈上，想必令他痛苦不堪。

column1: Gawaine is very ill and weak.  He must go back to Camelot and be tended by a healer at once, or he will die here, but he will never make it back on foot.
column2: 高文病重體弱，必須立刻回肯萊特由醫者診治，否則便會死在此地；但他絕無可能徒步走回去。

column1: The Black Knight has taken his life. Aye, well you should tremble at the sight. This crime lies heavily upon your own soul and will never be cleansed, no matter how you seek to right it.
column2: 黑武士已取走他的性命。是的，你見此情景理當心驚。這樁罪責將沉沉壓在你自己的靈魂之上，無論你如何試圖彌補，都永難洗清。

column1: Alas, Gawaine, the noble Gawaine is dead.   Perhaps he died of his injuries, but I fear it was your indifference that struck the final blow.
column2: 唉，高文，高貴的高文死了。或許他是傷重不治，但我擔心，真正給予最後一擊的，是你的漠然。

column1: He has returned to Camelot for healing.
column2: 他已回到肯萊特接受療傷。

column1: Though he is cut and bleeding, I fear his most serious injuries may not be as obvious to the eye.
column2: 雖然他身上有傷口在流血，但我擔心他最嚴重的傷勢，未必是肉眼能看得出來的。

column1: Does it matter how he died, be it of injuries or grief that his own king betrayed him?  He is dead.
column2: 他究竟是死於傷勢，還是死於得知自己的王背叛了他的哀痛，這重要嗎？他已經死了。

column1: It is a huge tree.
column2: 這是一株巨樹。

column1: Your horse has disappeared. It must have went back to Camelot.
column2: 你的坐騎已經消失了，想必是自行回了肯萊特。

column1: I cannot believe such filth... from the lips of my own king!
column2: 我不敢相信……這等污穢之言，竟出自我王之口！

column1: The smell of blood, sweat and illness is nearly overwhelming.
column2: 血腥、汗臭與病氣的味道幾乎令人難以承受。

column1: I fear... I am not... my usual fragrant self.
column2: 恐怕……我此刻……並非平日那般芬芳。

column1: The odor of human death is not a pleasant one.
column2: 人之將死所散發的氣味，並不好聞。

column1: I am disturbed by the labored quality of Gawaine's breathing.  He must reach Camelot as quickly as possible.
column2: 高文那沉重艱難的呼吸令我不安，他必須儘快抵達肯萊特。

column1: The pall of solemn death enshrouds this place.
column2: 一股肅穆的死亡氣息籠罩著此地。

column1: Sir Gawaine needs more than trivialities.
column2: 高文爵士所需要的，遠不止這些瑣碎之物。

column1: He is nearby.
column2: 他就在附近。

column1: You are the only one who can help him.  If he does not reach Camelot quickly, he will die.
column2: 唯有你能幫助他。他若不能盡快抵達肯萊特，便將喪命。

column1: It is too late for that.  Gawaine is dead.
column2: 那已為時已晚，高文已經死了。

column1: Concern yourself with such things after you have freed Gawaine from his suffering.
column2: 待你解救高文脫離苦難之後，再去掛心這些事吧。

column1: All the money in the world will not restore Sir Gawaine to life.
column2: 縱有天下所有的財富，也無法使高文爵士死而復生。

column1: Nay, m'lord.  I will not take....your money....for you may yet need it.
column2: 不，吾王。我不會收下……你的錢……你日後或許還用得著。

column1: Gawaine needs no gift so greatly as he needs the gift of healing, which you cannot give him, I fear.
column2: 高文最需要的，莫過於痊癒這份禮物，恐怕那並非你所能給予的。

column1: It is of no use to a dead man.
column2: 這東西對死者毫無用處。

column1: It can do nothing for Gawaine.
column2: 這對高文於事無補。

column1: What morbid thoughts.
column2: 好陰鬱的念頭。

column1: It cannot wash the stain of Gawaine's death from your soul.  He will be enfolded into the body of mother earth and this ancient tree shall be his monument.
column2: 這洗不去高文之死在你靈魂上留下的污點。他將回歸大地之母的懷抱，這株古樹便是他的紀念碑。

column1: For what you have allowed to happen, there can be no forgiveness.
column2: 對於你所縱容發生的事，沒有寬恕可言。

column1: You have no need of forgiveness. Your virtue, at the moment, is intact.
column2: 你不需要寬恕。此刻，你的德行仍完好無損。

column1: You do not have your mule.
column2: 你的騾子不在你身邊。

column1: Nothing can help him until he is free of the shackles.
column2: 除非先解開鎖鏈，否則什麼都幫不了他。

column1: Only the healers of Camelot can save him, if he can reach them in time.  He will never make it back on foot.
column2: 唯有肯萊特的醫者能救他，前提是他能及時抵達。他絕無可能徒步走回去。

column1: Have no fear. Gawaine will be tended well in Camelot.
column2: 不必擔憂，高文在肯萊特會受到妥善照料。

column1: My, your memory is short. You have already shattered the shackles.
column2: 哎呀，你的記性可真差，你早已打碎那鎖鏈了。

column1: Nothing you do now can restore Sir Gawaine to life.
column2: 你此刻做什麼，都無法讓高文爵士死而復生。

column1: You have dealt with the shackles.
column2: 你已經處理過那副鎖鏈了。

column1: These shackles do not unlock.
column2: 這副鎖鏈並無鎖孔可開。

column1: I am sure you will find a way.
column2: 我相信你會想出辦法的。

column1: The shackles are securely anchored.  Can you think of nothing better to try.
column2: 這副鎖鏈固定得十分牢靠，你就想不出更好的辦法嗎？

column1: Not all the sword brandishing in the world will return Gawaine to life. Be still.
column2: 縱使揮盡天下劍術，也無法使高文死而復生，且靜下心來吧。

column1: There is no danger for the moment. Best to put up your sword lest it make Gawaine uneasy.
column2: 此刻並無危險，還是收起你的劍為好，免得讓高文心生不安。

column1: There is no danger for the moment. Or did you have some other purpose in drawing your sword?
column2: 此刻並無危險。還是說，你拔劍另有別的用意？

column1: This is one place where it would be best to use your sword on foot.
column2: 這是個最好徒步持劍應戰的地方。

column1: There is no danger here. Be more specific about what non-violent use you portend.
column2: 此處並無危險。請說明白些，你打算做何種非暴力的用途。

column1: Help me, Arthur. The pain....is terrible.
column2: 救救我，亞瑟。這痛楚……難以忍受。

column1: Beware....the Mad Monk....of Glastonbury.
column2: 小心……格列斯登伯利的……瘋僧侶。

column1: I believe he has....the Grail.
column2: I believe he has....the Grail.

column1: Sir Gawaine shall never speak again.
column2: Sir Gawaine shall never speak again.

column1: Consider how you might best do that.
column2: Consider how you might best do that.

column1: Aye, Gawaine must be helped. If he does not reach Camelot soon, he will die of his injuries.
column2: Aye, Gawaine must be helped. If he does not reach Camelot soon, he will die of his injuries.

column1: He is beyond help.
column2: He is beyond help.

column1: First, you must dismount.
column2: First, you must dismount.

column1: Uh... surely you have mistaken me... for someone else.
column2: Uh... surely you have mistaken me... for someone else.

column1: Do not add necrophilia to your list of sins.
column2: Do not add necrophilia to your list of sins.

column1: Have you gone completely mad!?!

column1: ST. LEONARD'S FOREST\nIt is said that here the holy hermit, St. Leonard, did slay a most fearsome dragon. Where the saint's blood fell upon the ground, lillies-of-the-valley sprouted and flourished in his honor.

column1: WINDSOR\nThese fertile hunting grounds have long been protected by Cernunnos, Celtic god of the underworld. He has large stag's antlers upon his head and wears a golden torc about his neck.

column1: OT MOOR\nThough the waters of the moor are not deep, they are reputed to have healing powers. This is where the Lady of the Lake currently dwells. Her wisdom and power rivals my own.

column1: AVEBURY\nOn this site stands the largest of the stone circles, the remains of an ancient place of worship. It is surrounded by a bank and ditch with a diameter of 1400 ft. The circle is formed of almost 100 megaliths, some weighing up to 60 tons.

column1: MOTTISTONE\nUpon the Isle of Wight, Druid priests are reputed to have sacrificed white bulls. In this place are two great stones: an upright stone representing their God and a horizontal stone representing their Goddess. Mottistone means "the speaker's stone".

column1: BATH\nOver 800 years before the birth of Christ, Prince Bladud, son of a king, contracted the dread disease of leprosy. Unable to remain in human company, he turned to tending swine, but they, too, caught the disease. One day the swine ran wild and plunged into the dark, foul-smelling waters of a bog. When Bladud pulled them out, he discovered that the waters had healed both the animals and himself. The healing waters of Bath are famous to this day.

column1: KEYNSHAM\nA 6th century prince of Wales named Braglan had a daughter named Keyne. She came to a town wherein the lord gave her a piece of land that she might preach Christianity, but the land was heavily infested with large, venomous snakes. She at once turned the snakes into stone. She is remembered as St. Keyne and the town is named after her.

St. Swithun took pity upon her and made the eggs whole again. Or so they say.

column1: GLASTONBURY TOR\nThis hill has been revered for countless centuries. To the Celts, it was Ynys-Witrin, the Island of Glass, so-called because the lands around it were often flooded. It is also said that Joseph of Arimathea, who supervised the burial of Jesus, brought the Grail here and that where he stuck his staff into the ground, a Holy Thorn tree grew. Many religious orders have since come and gone and left their ruins behind. To reach the tor now, one must travel through the Forest Perilous.

column1: SHAPWICK\nSt. Indractus, along with his sister, Drusa and other pilgrims, were passing through here on their way back to Ireland from Rome. They were carrying bags of seed corn to give to the poor. Saxon outlaws murdered them, thinking their bags were filled with gold. The crime was discovered when a beam of light shone for 3 days and 3 nights upon the burial pit. Confronted with their deed, the Saxons went mad and destroyed one another.

column1: HALSTOCK\nA pious woman, St. Juthware, would open her house to pilgrims on their way to a nearby shrine. This so enraged her brother that he took up his sword and cut off her head. The story says that Juthware picked up her own head and carried it to the local altar before she finally died.

column1: BRAUNTON\nMany miracles dealing with animals are connected to St. Brannoc, who reportedly sailed from Wales in a stone coffin. A sow and piglets showed him where to establish his chapel. He used wild deer to pull his plough and taught the natives how to till soil. He brought back to life a cow which had been stolen from him, killed and dismembered, but at his call it reassembled itself and returned to give him milk for the rest of its life.

column1: EXETER\nJust outside this city is a well and a chapel dedicated to St. Sidwell. Sidwell was a girl who had inherited some land that her stepmother wanted.
